title: DE-VJEPA: Decision-Equivalent Latent Prediction for Policy Fidelity and Control
abstract: Accurate latent predictions need not preserve a controller's decisions, and preserving those decisions need not improve task success. We study these relationships through DE-VJEPA, which augments deterministic latent regression with a Kullback–Leibler (KL) penalty between a frozen reference policy's action distributions at observed and predicted future representations. The reported comparisons use a frozen ResNet-18 encoder on five MetaWorld tasks and PushT, with evaluation policies trained using different seeds. On clean MetaWorld, the policy-regularized predictor has 15.4% higher latent mean squared error but 19.8% lower decision KL than the latent-only baseline, reversing the model ranking. Decision KL improves in seven of eight dataset–condition comparisons, and its advantage persists through five-step prediction under recorded actions. Reference-policy and action-mean ablations probe the supervision signal; persistence remains a stronger baseline on clean PushT. Across 14,850 closed-loop MetaWorld episodes, however, the tested planners do not establish an aggregate success advantage over latent-only prediction. These findings distinguish latent accuracy, policy fidelity, and control performance as separate evaluation criteria and show the limits of using offline policy agreement to infer control benefits.
submission_type: Regular submission (no more than 12 pages of main content)
implementation_scope: Deterministic h=0 prediction path; posterior receives only its KL regularizer. The VJEPA/DE-VJEPA result labels are retained release identifiers.
